hint: Curve control points… · Example: Curve 0,0,0 50,100,0 100,0,0
Close · joins the polyline or curve being drawn back to its first point
Trim · pick objects, Enter, pick cutters, Enter, click the parts to remove · Esc cancels · Trim 0.2 0.8 keeps that part of a curve
Extend · pick boundaries, Enter, click near curve ends · Extend Distance 5 grows ends by a length · Extend -0.2 1.2 extends a curve's domain
Explode · a polyline into lines, a BRep into faces, a mesh into faces, a point cloud into points
Move · pick a base point, then the target point · Move 10,0,0 moves by a typed offset
Rotate · pick the center, then type an angle or pick two reference points · Rotate z 45 turns about a world axis
Scale · pick the origin, then type a factor or pick two reference points · 1D, 2D or 3D · Scale 2 scales at once
Copy · pick a base point, then as many target points as copies · Enter finishes · Copy 10,0,0 copies once
Orient 3 Points · pick three reference points, then three target points · the selection moves rigidly
Select a curve or face · Split · choose cutter curves · Enter confirms · Esc cancels
Save downloads the complete editable scene as a .session file
Open restores a saved .session file
Fit zooms to the selection, or the whole scene when nothing is selected
Layers (On Off All): show or hide the layer panel; All shows it with every row expanded
Opacity 0..1: how solid the faces are · 0 is x-ray, 1 solid · Example: Opacity 0.5
Arrowhead: heads on the selected lines, polylines and curves · None, Start, End or Both · Example: Arrowhead End
Element Attributes (On Off): show or hide the objects hung under each element, such as its base plane
Element Interactions (On Off): draw or remove what other elements do to each element, its contacts, joints and cuts
Element Plate: pick closed polylines, the outlines · Thickness 60 or a number changes it · Enter creates a plate on each · Element Plate 40 on a selection creates at once

Element Beam: pick lines or polylines, the axes · Width 150, Height 250 or two numbers change them · Enter creates a beam on each, mitred at its corners · Element Beam 120 200 on a selection creates at once
Element Column: pick lines, the axes · Width 200, Depth 300 or two numbers change them · Enter creates a column on each · Element Column 200 300 on a selection creates at once
Element Block: pick closed polylines, bottom then top, then hole pairs in the same order · Enter creates the block · on a selection it creates at once
Element Beam Variable: pick closed sections in station order · Enter creates the beam, its axis from the first section's centre to the last's · on a selection it creates at once
Element Support: pick points or planes, where the supports stand · Enter creates a support on each · on a selection it creates at once
Snap (On Off): snapping · Snap End / Near / Mid / Center / Perp toggles one kind
Grid Snap (On Off) or a spacing: a point off every object lands on the grid of the construction plane, 1000 apart at start like the ground grid's cells · Example: Grid Snap 50

Construction Plane XY / XZ / YZ fixes the plane points land on and the grid lies on · 3 Point picks its origin, a point on its x axis and one on its y side · View follows the view again · Example: Construction Plane 3 Point 0,0,0 1000,0,1000 0,1000,0
Arctic (On Off): soft contact shading, studio lighting and outlines
Outline (On Off): black surface outlines
Select Lasso · drag a loop around objects · Shift adds · Ctrl removes · Esc cancels

hint: Select Small length · selects visible objects whose bounding-box diagonal is shorter, in scene units · Example: Select Small 10

Clipping Plane: an origin, then a point on the side to cut away · 3Point · XY / YZ / ZX through a point · On / Off every cut · Flip the selected plane · Fill Hatch / Solid (default) · Example: Clipping Plane XY 0,0,1200
Box (Brep Mesh): base center, corner or length and width, height · Example: Box 0,0,0 100 50 30
Sphere (Brep Mesh): center, radius · Example: Sphere 0,0,0 10
Cylinder (Brep Mesh): base center, radius, height · Example: Cylinder 0,0,0 5 20
Cone (Brep Mesh): base center, radius, height to the apex · Example: Cone 0,0,0 5 20
Pyramid (Brep Mesh): base center, corner or edge length, height · Example: Pyramid 0,0,0 10 15
Torus (Brep Mesh): center, major radius, minor radius · Example: Torus 0,0,0 20 5
Block With Hole (Brep Mesh): base center, corner or length and width, height, hole radius · Example: Block With Hole 0,0,0 40 30 20 5
Tetrahedron (Brep Mesh): center, radius to the corners · Example: Tetrahedron 0,0,0 10
Octahedron (Brep Mesh): center, radius to the corners · Example: Octahedron 0,0,0 10
Dodecahedron (Brep Mesh): center, radius to the corners · Example: Dodecahedron 0,0,0 10
Icosahedron (Brep Mesh): center, radius to the corners · Example: Icosahedron 0,0,0 10
Quad Sphere (Mesh): center, radius · six patches of 8 × 8 quads · Example: Quad Sphere 0,0,0 10
Capsule (Mesh): base center, radius, total height · Example: Capsule 0,0,0 5 30
Nurbs Curve Circle: center, radius · Example: Nurbs Curve Circle 0,0,0 10
Nurbs Curve Ellipse: center, end of the first axis or its radius, second radius · Example: Nurbs Curve Ellipse 0,0,0 20 10
Nurbs Curve Arc (Center 3 Points): center, start or radius, end or angle · Example: Nurbs Curve Arc 0,0,0 10 90
Nurbs Curve Parabola: start, end or length, apex or height · Example: Nurbs Curve Parabola 0,0,0 100 40
Loft (Open Closed): click curves in section order, Enter lofts · Example: select curves, then Loft Closed
Extrude (Cap On Cap Off): curves, Enter, then a distance or x,y,z · Example: select curves, then Extrude 25
Nurbs Surface Loft (Smooth Straight): click curves in section order, Enter lofts
Nurbs Surface Network: click curves of both directions in any order, Enter builds the surface through them
Nurbs Surface Revolve: profile curves, Enter, axis start, axis end, angle · Example: Nurbs Surface Revolve 0,0,0 0,0,1 90
Nurbs Surface 4 Points: four corners in order · Example: Nurbs Surface 4 Points 0,0,0 10,0,0 10,10,3 0,10,0
Nurbs Surface Sweep1: the rail, then profile curves, Enter sweeps
Nurbs Surface Sweep2: first rail, second rail, shape curves, Enter sweeps

Project To Plane: flatten the selected points, lines, polylines, curves and meshes · CPlane is the plane the view faces · XY / YZ / ZX through the origin · 3Point picks the plane · Example: Project To Plane XY
Measure Distance · pick two points, snaps on · or type Measure Distance 0,0,0 100,0,0
Length · total length of the selected lines, polylines and NURBS curves
BoundingBox · create a world axis aligned box around the selection
Length BoundingBox · world X, Y and Z extents of the selection
Area · surface area of the selected meshes, BReps, NURBS surfaces and elements, or of one selected face
Volume · volume of the selected closed meshes, solid BReps and elements; open ones are refused
Add Group [name] · put the selection under a new group node; a click on one member then selects them all
Add Edge · connect the two selected objects in the session graph; the Graph table of the layers panel lists it
